notes:
Input cache text was an SPSS PROCESS output for Study 1, not the titled replication paper or assigned Study 2; frozen cache left unchanged. Independently obtained the matching published replication paper from the authors’ website, including supplementary materials. Success vocabulary successful maps the authors’ qualified verdict mostly successful; authors report four of eight sets supporting predictions. Effect and p left null because the neutral description and Table 9 locator do not distinguish eight key contrasts; no arbitrary row selected. Original acquisition: DOI landing abstract/robots denial; CMU indexed PDF redirected to directory; OpenAlex no best OA location and legacy author PDF returned 404. Original statistics reported retrospectively in replication Table 13 were not substituted for original-paper extraction.
Source follow-up: Verified published article title and authors against supplied reference. Numerical target pages were visually checked against the scanned PDF, retaining the published version. Experiment 1 reports 184 volunteers overall on printed p. 546, with groups of 24 to 37; Table 1 covers Experiments 1 and 2 and reports sample sizes varying from 24 to 41. Neither supplies an identified combined analytic n for the broad target. Table 1 contains separate outcome-specific comparisons and significance thresholds, not a uniquely identified test for the supplied description. Results also provide descriptive average probabilities across three scenarios; no corresponding omnibus effect size/test statistic and p are printed there. Therefore no test-specific n, effect size, or p is selected or calculated. The source is available; the unresolved issue is locator specificity. Replication and reported_success intentionally remain unassigned placeholders.
